title: Best Fast Food for a Hangover: Chain-by-Chain Picks That Help
excerpt: The best fast food for a hangover, chain by chain: what to order at McDonald's, Chick-fil-A, Taco Bell, Chipotle, Wendy's and more, what to drink with it, and what to skip.
metaDescription: The best fast food for a hangover, chain by chain: what to order at McDonalds, Chick-fil-A, Taco Bell, Chipotle and more, plus what to drink and skip.
author: DHM Guide Team
content:
**The honest answer first:** the best fast food for a hangover is a meal that gives you salt, some protein, easy carbohydrates, and a big drink of water, without so much grease that it upsets a stomach that's already irritated. In practice that usually means an egg-based breakfast sandwich, a chicken sandwich or grilled nuggets, a burrito bowl, or a cup of soup or chili, paired with water or an electrolyte drink instead of a giant soda or coffee on an empty stomach. No drive-thru order cures a hangover. But the right one can make the next few hours noticeably easier, and the wrong one can make your stomach worse.

**The quick picks:** at McDonald's, an Egg McMuffin and hash brown with water. At Chick-fil-A, grilled nuggets or a chicken biscuit plus chicken noodle soup. At Taco Bell, a breakfast burrito or a bean burrito. At Chipotle, a bowl with rice, beans, chicken, and salsa. At Wendy's, a cup of chili and a baked potato. At Panera, any brothy soup with bread. Anywhere you go, add a large water first and drink it before the food arrives.

> **When to see a doctor:** A normal hangover is miserable but passes within about a day. Food won't fix the following, and they need medical attention. **Get help if** you can't keep any fluids down for several hours, you're vomiting blood or something that looks like coffee grounds, you have severe stomach pain that doesn't ease, you're confused or very hard to wake, you're breathing slowly or irregularly, or you have a seizure. Those can be signs of alcohol poisoning, dehydration that needs IV fluids, or a stomach problem such as bleeding or pancreatitis. If you ever get shaking, sweating, a racing heart, or seeing things that aren't there when you *stop* drinking after a long stretch of heavy daily drinking, that's alcohol withdrawal, not a hangover, and it needs a doctor the same day. In an emergency, call 911.

## Why Food Helps a Hangover at All

It helps to know what you're actually trying to fix, because "soak up the alcohol" is not it. By the morning after, most or all of the alcohol has already been absorbed and processed. A burger can't pull it back out of your bloodstream. What food can do is help with some of the side effects alcohol left behind.

Here's what's going on in a typical hangover, in plain terms:

- **You're short on fluid and salt.** Alcohol blocks a hormone called vasopressin, which normally tells your kidneys to hold onto water. So you urinate more than you drink, and you lose sodium and potassium with it. That's a big part of the headache, thirst, and lightheaded feeling.
- **Your blood sugar may be low.** Your liver is busy processing alcohol overnight, which can interfere with how it releases glucose. Especially if you skipped dinner, you can wake up shaky, weak, and foggy, and carbohydrates help with that.
- **Your stomach lining is irritated.** Alcohol increases stomach acid and inflames the lining. That's why you feel queasy and why some foods sit badly.
- **Your body is dealing with inflammation and poor sleep.** Alcohol triggers an inflammatory response and breaks up deep sleep. Food doesn't fix either directly, but being fed and hydrated makes the rest of the day more manageable.

So a good hangover meal does four things: replaces salt and fluid, raises blood sugar gently, gives you some protein so the energy lasts, and stays easy on the stomach. That's the lens for every pick below.

It's also worth being upfront about the evidence. There is no good evidence that any particular food, fast food or otherwise, shortens a hangover. Researchers who study hangovers have tested a lot of remedies, and very few hold up. The advice here is based on what each part of a meal does for dehydration, blood sugar, and a sore stomach, which is solid physiology, not on proof that a specific sandwich works.

## What to Look For on Any Fast Food Menu

You won't always be near the chain you want. These rules work anywhere.

**Order more of:**

- **Eggs.** Easy protein, cheap, and on nearly every breakfast menu. Eggs contain cysteine, an amino acid that has been studied in lab work for its role in breaking down acetaldehyde, the toxic by-product of alcohol. That research is early, so treat eggs as good, easy protein rather than a cure. Our guide to [eggs for a hangover](/never-hungover/eggs-for-hangover) goes into the details.
- **Lean protein.** Grilled chicken, turkey, beans, or a single-patty burger. Protein helps steady your energy after the carbs kick in.
- **Plain starches.** Toast, English muffins, rice, potatoes, tortillas, crackers, and bread are gentle and raise blood sugar without much fat.
- **Salt and broth.** Soup, chili, and salty sides like a single hash brown or a pickle help replace sodium. Broth adds fluid at the same time.
- **Fruit and juice in modest amounts.** Orange juice or a fruit cup brings potassium, fluid, and fast sugar. Bananas, where they're sold, are an easy potassium source too.

**Go easy on:**

- **Very greasy, fried, or large meals.** A double bacon cheeseburger with large fries is a lot of fat for an inflamed stomach. Fat slows how fast your stomach empties, which can make nausea worse.
- **Spicy food** if your stomach is unsettled. Hot sauce, spicy chicken, and jalapeños can aggravate heartburn.
- **Huge sodas and milkshakes.** A large regular soda is a lot of sugar in one go, which can lead to a spike and a crash. Diet soda isn't harmful, but it doesn't rehydrate as well as water or an electrolyte drink.
- **Coffee on an empty stomach.** Coffee can help the headache and grogginess if you're a regular drinker of it, but it's acidic. Have it with food, not instead of food.
- **"Hair of the dog."** A beer or mimosa with brunch only delays the hangover. It doesn't treat it.

## Is Greasy Food Good for a Hangover?

This is the question most people are really asking. The honest answer is: greasy food helps more *before* drinking than *after*.

Eating a meal with fat and protein before or while you drink slows down how fast alcohol moves from your stomach into your small intestine, which is where most of it gets absorbed. That means a lower, slower peak in blood alcohol. That effect is well established, and it's the reason a big dinner before a night out is a good idea. Our guide on [what to eat before drinking](/never-hungover/what-to-eat-before-drinking-alcohol-evidence-based-guide) covers it in detail.

The morning after, the alcohol is already processed. Grease can't absorb it. What greasy food does offer is salt, calories, and comfort, and those aren't nothing. Many people genuinely feel better after a bacon, egg, and cheese sandwich. The catch is that very fatty food is harder to digest, and if you're nauseous it can sit in your stomach and make things worse.

A sensible middle ground: if your stomach feels fine and you're craving something greasy, a moderate portion is fine. Get one breakfast sandwich, not two plus a large side of fries. If you feel queasy, skip the fried stuff and go for toast, a plain burrito, rice, or soup first. You can always eat more later. There's more on this in our deep dive on [greasy food and hangovers](/never-hungover/greasy-food-hangover).

## Best Fast Food for a Hangover: Chain-by-Chain Picks

Menus change by region and over time, so if an item below has been dropped near you, use the rules above to pick its closest substitute. These picks are based on what each item brings to the table (salt, protein, carbs, fluid, and how gentle it is), not on any hangover testing.

### McDonald's for a hangover

McDonald's is often the closest option, and its breakfast menu works well.

- **Best pick: Egg McMuffin.** An egg, Canadian bacon, and cheese on an English muffin. It has protein, salt, and a plain starch, and it's one of the less greasy breakfast sandwiches on any fast food menu.
- **Good add-on: hash brown.** One hash brown brings salt and comfort. It's fried, so one is plenty.
- **Gentle option: oatmeal.** McDonald's fruit and maple oatmeal is easy on a nauseous stomach and gives you slow-release carbs.
- **Drink: water and orange juice.** OJ for potassium and quick sugar, water for fluid.
- **Go easy on:** the big breakfast platters and the sausage-and-biscuit combos if your stomach is unsettled. They're heavy.

If it's after breakfast hours, a plain hamburger or cheeseburger and a small fries is a reasonable choice, with a large water. A single patty is easier to handle than a double or triple.

### Chick-fil-A for a hangover

Chick-fil-A has some of the best hangover options among the big chains because it sells soup and grilled chicken alongside the fried stuff.

- **Best pick: chicken noodle soup.** Broth, salt, noodles, and chicken. It gives you fluid, sodium, carbs, and protein in one cup, and it's very gentle.
- **Strong pick: grilled nuggets.** Lean protein without the fryer oil.
- **Breakfast pick: chicken biscuit or Egg White Grill.** The biscuit is more comforting; the Egg White Grill is lighter.
- **Side: fruit cup.** Fluid and some natural sugar.
- **Go easy on:** a large fried meal with waffle fries and a milkshake if you're queasy.

### Taco Bell for a hangover

Taco Bell is a late-night favorite for a reason. Plain carbs and beans go a long way.

- **Best pick: a breakfast burrito or breakfast crunchwrap**, if your location serves breakfast. Eggs and a tortilla are a good base.
- **Strong pick: bean burrito.** Beans give you protein, fiber, and some potassium, and the tortilla gives you gentle carbs. It's cheap and not very greasy.
- **Good option: a chicken burrito bowl or soft chicken taco.**
- **Go easy on:** extra-spicy sauces and the heaviest cheese-loaded items if you have heartburn or an upset stomach.

### Chipotle for a hangover

Chipotle lets you build exactly the meal you need, which makes it one of the better hangover choices.

- **Best build: a bowl with white rice, black or pinto beans, chicken, mild salsa, and lettuce.** Plenty of carbs, protein, and salt, without much grease.
- **Add:** a bag of chips if you want extra salt.
- **Go easy on:** hot salsa, a big scoop of sour cream and cheese, and queso if your stomach is touchy.

Chipotle doesn't do breakfast at most locations, so this is a lunch-time pick.

### Wendy's for a hangover

Wendy's has two underrated hangover items: chili and baked potatoes.

- **Best pick: a cup of chili.** Beans, meat, tomato, salt, and some liquid. It's filling without being greasy.
- **Strong pick: a plain or sour cream and chive baked potato.** A gentle starch that also brings potassium.
- **Breakfast pick:** a breakfast sandwich with egg, where your location serves breakfast.
- **Go easy on:** the large bacon-heavy burgers.

### Panera for a hangover

If you can make it to a sit-down-style fast casual spot, Panera is one of the easiest on the stomach.

- **Best pick: a brothy soup**, such as chicken noodle, with a side of bread or a baguette. Fluid, sodium, and gentle carbs.
- **Breakfast pick:** an egg sandwich on a bagel or ciabatta.
- **Go easy on:** very creamy soups if you're nauseous. They're heavier than broth.

### Subway for a hangover

Subway is a good choice when you want something lighter but still filling.

- **Best pick: a turkey or rotisserie-style chicken sub on plain bread**, with lettuce, tomato, a few pickles, and a light sauce. Pickles add a bit of salt, which is one reason people swear by [pickle juice for hangovers](/never-hungover/pickle-juice-for-hangover).
- **Breakfast pick:** an egg-based breakfast sub where available.
- **Go easy on:** spicy sauces and a footlong packed with salami and extra cheese.

### Dunkin' and Starbucks for a hangover

Coffee shops are where a lot of hungover mornings start. Just don't make it coffee only.

- **Dunkin':** a Wake-Up Wrap or an egg and cheese on an English muffin, plus a bottle of water. Have coffee only with the food.
- **Starbucks:** egg bites, a breakfast sandwich, or a plain bagel, plus water. Oatmeal is also a gentle choice.
- **Go easy on:** a large sweet coffee drink on an empty stomach, which is a lot of sugar and acid at once.

### Burger King, Jack in the Box, Sonic, and similar burger chains

The same logic applies across the burger chains.

- **Best picks:** a breakfast sandwich with egg in the morning, or a single-patty burger later in the day.
- **Sides:** one small fries or hash browns, not a large.
- **Drink:** water first. If you want something sweet, a small juice or lemonade beats a large soda.

### Waffle House and diners

Not exactly fast food, but often open when you need it.

- **Best picks:** scrambled eggs, toast, hash browns, and a side of fruit or juice. A classic plate covers protein, carbs, and salt.
- **Go easy on:** piling on gravy, sausage, and bacon all at once if your stomach is unsettled.

### Pho, ramen, and noodle shops

If you have one nearby, a bowl of noodle soup is one of the best hangover meals you can buy. It's warm, salty, full of fluid, and gentle on the stomach, with carbs from the noodles and protein from the meat or egg. Pho in particular is a hangover tradition in a lot of cities for good reason. Go light on chili oil and sriracha if your stomach is touchy. For more on why soups work, see our guide to the [best soups for a hangover](/never-hungover/best-soups-for-hangover).

## Best Fast Food Breakfast for a Hangover

Breakfast menus are usually the best bet, because they're built around eggs, toast, potatoes, and juice. Ranked roughly from gentlest to heaviest:

| Pick | Where to find it | Why it works | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Oatmeal | McDonald's, Starbucks, Panera | Very gentle, slow-release carbs | Not much protein or salt on its own |
| Egg on an English muffin | McDonald's, Dunkin', Starbucks | Protein, salt, plain starch, not much grease | Little fluid, so pair with water |
| Egg bites or Egg White Grill | Starbucks, Chick-fil-A | Lean protein, easy to eat | Small; may need a carb side |
| Breakfast burrito | Taco Bell, many local spots | Eggs plus a tortilla, filling | Skip extra-spicy sauce if queasy |
| Chicken biscuit | Chick-fil-A, others | Comforting, salty, filling | Fried, so stop at one |
| Bacon, egg, and cheese on a biscuit or croissant | Most chains | Salt and calories | Heavier; can upset a sore stomach |

Whatever you order, add water and, if you like it, a small orange juice. The juice helps with blood sugar and potassium. If you'd rather cook at home, our guide to the [best hangover breakfast](/never-hungover/best-hangover-breakfast) has simple recipes.

## What to Drink With Your Order

Your drink matters as much as your food. Dehydration drives a lot of hangover symptoms, and most fast food orders don't contain much water.

- **Water first.** Ask for a large cup of water and drink some before the food arrives. It's free at most chains.
- **Electrolyte drinks if you're really depleted.** If you've been sweating, vomiting, or you just feel wrung out, a sports drink or an oral rehydration drink replaces sodium and potassium along with fluid. Many gas stations next to drive-thrus carry them. Our [electrolyte drinks comparison](/never-hungover/electrolyte-drinks-for-hangover-compared) explains which ones have meaningful amounts of salt.
- **Orange juice in a small size.** Good for potassium and quick sugar.
- **Coffee with food, not instead of it.** If you drink coffee every day, skipping it can add a caffeine-withdrawal headache to your hangover. Have your usual amount with breakfast.
- **Skip the extra-large soda.** It's not dangerous, but it's a big sugar load and not great for hydration.
- **Skip alcohol.** A "hair of the dog" drink postpones the hangover rather than ending it.

## Fast Food to Avoid With a Hangover

Nothing on a menu is off-limits for a healthy person, but some choices make a hangover worse for many people:

- **Very large, very greasy meals.** Doubles and triples, loaded fries, and big fried platters can make nausea worse because fat slows down how fast your stomach empties.
- **Very spicy food.** Spicy wings, hot sauces, and spicy chicken sandwiches can aggravate heartburn and an irritated stomach.
- **Huge sugary drinks and shakes on their own.** You get a fast spike and then a slump, without the protein or salt you need.
- **Eating too much too fast.** If you're nauseous, start with a few bites of something plain and some water, wait, then eat more.

If nausea is your main problem, start with crackers, toast, a plain bun, rice, or broth, and work up from there. Our [hangover nausea guide](/never-hungover/hangover-nausea-complete-guide-fast-stomach-relief-2025) has more ways to settle your stomach.

## Late-Night Fast Food: Does Eating Before Bed Help?

A lot of fast food gets ordered at 1 a.m. on the way home. Is that a good idea?

It can help a little, with limits. If you drank on an empty stomach, eating before bed gives your body some fuel overnight, which may soften the low-blood-sugar part of the next morning. It won't bring your blood alcohol down quickly, though. Food slows absorption of alcohol that is still in your stomach, but by the time you've finished drinking for the night, most of it has already been absorbed.

Two cautions:

- **Huge, greasy, spicy meals right before lying down are a recipe for heartburn and acid reflux.** If you eat late, keep it moderate and give yourself a little time before bed if you can.
- **Drink a big glass of water with it.** That does more for the next morning than the food itself.

A bean burrito, a plain burger, a chicken sandwich, or a cup of soup are all better late-night choices than a giant combo with a large soda.

## Fast Food vs. Home Remedies: What Actually Matters Most

It's easy to focus on which sandwich to buy, but the things that matter most for a hangover are simpler:

1. **How much you drank.** The size of a hangover tracks closely with how much alcohol you had. No food changes that.
2. **Fluid and salt.** Rehydrating well is one of the few things that reliably helps people feel better.
3. **Sleep.** Alcohol wrecks sleep quality. Rest is a big part of recovery.
4. **Eating something.** Food helps blood sugar and gives you energy, which is where fast food comes in.
5. **Time.** Most hangovers ease within 24 hours no matter what you eat.

So the fast food is helpful, but it's a supporting player. Pair it with water, rest, and, if you need one, a pain reliever taken with food. For a full view of foods with the best rationale behind them, see our guide to the [best foods for a hangover](/never-hungover/best-foods-for-hangover).

## A Simple Hangover Fast Food Game Plan

If you just want a plan to follow, use this:

1. **Before you order,** drink a large water.
2. **If you're nauseous,** start with something plain: toast, oatmeal, a plain burrito, rice, or broth-based soup.
3. **If your stomach is fine,** get an egg-based breakfast sandwich, a chicken sandwich, a burrito bowl, or a cup of chili.
4. **Add salt and potassium:** a single hash brown or small fries, a pickle, OJ, a banana, or an electrolyte drink.
5. **Keep it moderate.** One sandwich and one side. You can eat again in a couple of hours.
6. **Rest and keep sipping water** through the afternoon.

## Planning Ahead for Next Time

The best hangover meal is the one you eat *before* you drink. A proper dinner with protein, fat, and carbohydrates slows down how fast alcohol is absorbed, which helps more than anything you eat the next morning. Alternating alcohol with water, pacing yourself, and stopping earlier make the biggest difference of all. Our guide on [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) covers the habits with the best evidence.

Some people also add a supplement to their routine. **DHM (dihydromyricetin)** is a plant compound from the Japanese raisin tree that has been studied for its effects on alcohol metabolism and the liver. Most of the research is from animal and lab studies, and human evidence is still limited, so it's promising rather than proven. There is no good evidence that it replaces eating, hydrating, or drinking less. If you want to try it as part of a sensible plan, popular options include [No Days Wasted DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) and the budget-friendly [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20). Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) covers how much people typically take and when, and our [supplement reviews](/reviews) compare the main brands.

## The Bottom Line

- The best fast food for a hangover gives you salt, protein, gentle carbs, and fluid without a mountain of grease.
- Strong picks: an Egg McMuffin, Chick-fil-A chicken noodle soup or grilled nuggets, a Taco Bell bean or breakfast burrito, a Chipotle bowl, Wendy's chili and a baked potato, Panera broth soups, or a bowl of pho.
- Greasy food helps more before drinking than after. The morning after, keep fried food moderate, especially if you're queasy.
- Drink water or an electrolyte drink with your meal. It matters as much as the food.
- If you can't keep fluids down, have severe stomach pain, are vomiting blood, or are confused or hard to wake, that's not a normal hangover. Get medical help.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**What is the best fast food for a hangover?**

The best options combine salt, protein, gentle carbohydrates, and fluid without too much grease. Good examples are an egg breakfast sandwich like the Egg McMuffin, Chick-fil-A chicken noodle soup or grilled nuggets, a bean or breakfast burrito from Taco Bell, a Chipotle bowl with rice, beans, and chicken, or a cup of Wendy's chili. Pair any of them with a large water or an electrolyte drink. No fast food cures a hangover, but these give your body what it's short on.

**Is greasy food good for a hangover?**

Greasy food helps more before drinking than after. Fat and protein in your stomach slow how fast alcohol is absorbed, so a solid meal before a night out is a good idea. The next morning, the alcohol has already been processed, and grease can't soak it up. A moderate greasy breakfast can still be comforting and salty, but very fatty food can make nausea worse, so keep the portion reasonable if your stomach feels off.

**What should I get at McDonald's for a hangover?**

An Egg McMuffin is one of the best choices: an egg, Canadian bacon, and cheese on an English muffin gives you protein, salt, and plain carbs without too much grease. Add one hash brown for extra salt and a water plus a small orange juice to drink. If you're nauseous, the oatmeal is a gentler start. After breakfast hours, a plain single-patty burger with a small fries and water works well.

**Is Chick-fil-A good for a hangover?**

Yes, it's one of the better chains for a hangover because it sells chicken noodle soup and grilled nuggets. The soup gives you fluid, sodium, noodles, and chicken in one gentle cup. Grilled nuggets are lean protein without fryer oil. A chicken biscuit is a more comforting breakfast option. Add a fruit cup and water to round it out.

**Should I eat fast food before bed after drinking?**

A moderate snack before bed can help a little, especially if you drank on an empty stomach, because it gives your body fuel overnight. It won't sober you up, though, because most of the alcohol has already been absorbed by then. Avoid huge, spicy, or very greasy meals right before lying down, since they can trigger heartburn. Drinking a big glass of water with your late-night food does more for the next morning than the food itself.

**What fast food should I avoid with a hangover?**

Go easy on very large greasy meals, very spicy food, and giant sodas or milkshakes on their own. Fat slows down how fast your stomach empties, which can worsen nausea, and spicy food can aggravate heartburn. A big sugary drink gives you a spike and a slump without the salt or protein you need. Skip a "hair of the dog" drink too, since it only delays the hangover.

**What should I drink with fast food when hungover?**

Water first, ideally a large cup before your food arrives. If you feel very depleted or have been vomiting, an electrolyte or sports drink replaces sodium and potassium along with fluid. A small orange juice adds potassium and quick sugar. If you drink coffee daily, have your usual cup with food to avoid a caffeine-withdrawal headache, but don't use it as a substitute for water.

**When is a hangover serious enough to see a doctor?**

See a doctor or go to urgent care if you can't keep fluids down for several hours, are vomiting blood or material that looks like coffee grounds, have severe stomach pain, or feel faint when standing. Call 911 if someone is confused, very hard to wake, breathing slowly or irregularly, or has a seizure, since these can be signs of alcohol poisoning. Shaking, sweating, and a racing heart after stopping a long stretch of heavy daily drinking can be alcohol withdrawal and also need a doctor promptly.
